standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the left vertical components with stalks of F and supplies the injectivity of F_x -> Pi(F)_x.

core_obligations: The four maps are as listed in the statement: left vertical components via F#_x = F_x (statement line 1902, justified by the stalk-sheafification lemma), top and bottom horizontal maps from the canonical map F -> Pi(F) (statement lines 1904-1905 and 1915-1917), right vertical components the stalk maps of Pi(F) (statement lines 1907-1908). The diagram commutes since all maps are induced by the same presheaf map (proof line 1922). The bottom arrow is injective because each component F_x -> Pi(F)_x is injective, as established in the proof of the stalk-sheafification lemma (proof lines 1924-1928). Finally, s in Pi(F)(U) lies in F#(U) iff (*) holds, and (*) says s comes locally from sections of F, which by the definition of stalk functors is equivalent to the value of s in every stalk Pi(F)_x lying in the image of F_x -> Pi(F)_x (proof lines 1929-1934). This is exactly the fibre product condition (proof lines 1921-1934).
proof_roadmap: Fix the four maps and the commutativity of the square (statement lines 1900-1917, proof line 1922).
Prove injectivity of the bottom arrow and the fibre product condition via (*) translated to stalks (proof lines 1924-1934).
